Call highlights: 
- Primary workload: customer support assistant (chat + short context retrieval).
- Expected QPS: 120 requests/minute peak; average across business hours ~45 req/min.
- Concurrency: up to ~30 concurrent streaming sessions during peak.
- Latency targets: 95th percentile request latency <= 250ms for US, <= 300ms for EU, <= 400ms for APAC (these are customer-facing response times).
- Throughput requirement: sustain token generation of ~8,000 tokens/minute at peak.
- Streaming: yes — partial token streaming required for UI progressive rendering.

Hi Samir — quick technical responses inline to help scope the POC. Happy to expand in the follow-up call.

1) APAC latency & streaming: 
- Streaming adds ~20-80ms overhead depending on chunking and network RTT. For APAC we typically see higher RTTs; hitting P95 <= 400ms with streaming is achievable using a combination of: regionally-deployed model endpoints (APAC region), model quantization (int8/fp16), and aggressive batching thresholds for non-interactive paths.
- Recommendation: deploy an APAC endpoint for production if strict P95 targets are required. For the POC we can run APAC traffic through a regional endpoint in APAC (partner cloud region) or use a Dedicated capacity backfilled in APAC.

2) Regional routing & fallback: 
- Redwood supports policy-driven routing. You can configure preferred-region routing rules (geo-IP + user-region mapping) with tiered fallback. Fallbacks are visible in the console and surfaced in tracing logs.
- Failover behavior: when EU capacity is constrained we can failover to US with an explicit flag; we also support canary traffic percentages, and auto-fallback is auditable.

3) Data residency options: 
- Hosted Dedicated with regional isolation can satisfy many EU residency requirements (data-at-rest and logs kept in-region), but for strict regulatory regimes or non-export of raw logs, Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) is recommended.
- We can provide KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs for either option.

4) Concurrency & KV cache: 
- Concurrency per model instance depends on model size and GPU type. For typical LLM sizes used in your workload, a single QPS-optimized instance (A100/NVIDIA equivalent) can sustain ~6-10 concurrent streaming sessions with sub-250ms token latency under optimized kernels and batching.
- KV cache (prefix caching) dramatically reduces cold-starts for ongoing conversations and reduces token compute for repeated contexts — recommended for your workload.

POC proposal (technical): 
- Week 0-1: Provision US Dedicated capacity and baseline tests.
- Week 2: Bring up EU isolated Dedicated (or Private trial) and run EU latency tests.
- Week 3: Verify streaming performance, concurrency stress tests, and failover behavior.
- Week 4: Finalize SLO dashboard and handoff for production rollout.

I'll attach a short SLO feasibility note to the Drive folder.
